Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing call — Acme AI

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — really enjoyed the conversation and getting a sense of Acme AI's inference needs. Quick recap from our discovery so we're aligned before the sizing call: 

- Primary workload: customer-facing summarization and reranking for search results
- Current peak traffic you mentioned: ~120 req/s (bursts to ~150)
- Typical prompt size: ~450 tokens (avg), some up to ~1k tokens
- SLO targets you mentioned: p50 < 150ms, p95 ~300ms (want to firm up p99 objective)
- Compliance: SOC2 is in scope; data residency in us-east preferred

Proposed next step: schedule a dedicated capacity sizing call (tech deep-dive) where our solutions engineer can run through throughput/latency tradeoffs, model variants, and a preliminary GPU sizing. Suggested attendees: your engineering lead (for traffic patterns), any infra/ops folks we should include, and Nikhil from my team.

Available slots we have next week:
- Monday 6/28 11:00 AM PT
- Tuesday 6/29 9:00 AM PT (preferable for our infra team)

If you can confirm which slot works or propose alternatives, we'll send a calendar invite and a short prep checklist (sample workload CSV + example queries) to make the call most productive. If you can, please attach a short sample of peak/avg traffic by hour and an example prompt set.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0102

Attachments: sample_workload_template.csv (we'll send this if you don't have one)

Thanks — I'll join the deep dive. A few quick asks so we can come prepared: 

1) Priority: Is the main goal strict latency (p50/p95/p99) or maximizing throughput/cost efficiency? That drives batching and instance sizing.
2) Can you share expected concurrency and whether traffic is spiky (short bursts) or steady? The CSV helps but a short hour-by-hour peak example is ideal.
3) Any model constraints? (e.g., 70B vs 13B family, quantized variants ok, whether you need us to recommend model/quantization)
4) Compliance/region hard requirements beyond SOC2 and us-east?

On our side I'll bring a preliminary GPU sizing calc, tradeoff slides (latency vs batching), and notes on warm-cache behaviour (KV cache benefits for repeat prompts). If Tue 6/29 9:00 AM PT works for everyone, please confirm and I'll create the invite and attach a short prep doc.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
